name: fzf
summary: General-purpose fuzzy finder. Shell integration adds Ctrl-T (files), Ctrl-R (history), Alt-C (cd) and ** completion; fully themeable with --color.
configFormat: command-line options in env vars (FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS) or an options file (FZF_DEFAULT_OPTS_FILE); no config file by default
startupCostMs: Measured 2026-11-23, Windows 11, fzf 0.75.0 via scoop shim, median of 10: `fzf --bash` 37 ms vs `fzf --version` 34 ms vs an empty `cmd /c rem` 23 ms, so the init itself is ~3 ms and the cost is process spawn. Running `eval "$(fzf --bash)"` adds that spawn plus parsing ~1000 lines of shell on every shell start; cache the output to a file and `source` it (regenerate when the fzf binary is newer) to avoid the spawn.

windows.notes: fzf ships key bindings for bash, zsh, fish only. In Git Bash/MSYS2 bash they work. In PowerShell use the PSFzf module (PowerShell Gallery, MIT). cmd.exe has no integration.

install.notes: Ubuntu 24.04 ships 0.44.1, which has no `fzf --bash/--zsh` (added in 0.48.0); Debian 13 ships 0.60.3. On older distros install the release binary or source the scripts from the package examples directory (path unverified).

theme.notes: --color with hex or ANSI names, or the base16 scheme to follow the terminal palette.

integration.notes: fd as the walker, bat/eza previews, per-shell wiring.
